spec.title: Sum CLI
spec.goal: Build a Rust command-line tool that sums one or more decimal integers given as arguments, prints the total, and prints a short usage message with a non-zero exit when there are no arguments, an argument is not an integer, or the sum would overflow a 64-bit signed integer.
acceptance: One or more integer arguments print their sum.
Negative integers are accepted and summed correctly.
No arguments, or an argument that is not an integer, prints usage and exits non-zero.
A sum that would overflow `i64` prints a short error and exits non-zero instead of panicking.
Unit tests cover a valid sum, negative values, missing arguments, invalid input, and overflow.
constraints: Start from the reference template; keep its package metadata and lock file valid.
Tests must not touch the filesystem.
non_goals: No floats, flags, stdin input, or multiple operations.
context: The reference template at `templates/bin/` is the starting point.
This is the second task in the `sum-cli` project. `tasks/sum-cli` is the prior run and `lessons/sum-cli.md` holds its review lessons.
The prior task deliberately excluded overflow handling; this task adds it.

compiles.reason: cargo check: error[E0599]: no associated function or constant named `from_str` found for type `i64` in the current scope

revision_guidance: cargo check fails because i64::from_str needs FromStr in scope, and the argument slicing is inconsistent. Rewrite src/main.rs exactly this way. Keep const USAGE. In main: let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect(); then match parse_and_sum(&args) { Ok(sum) => println!("{}", sum), Err(err) => { eprintln!("{}", err); std::process::exit(1); } }. In parse_and_sum(args: &[String]) -> Result<i64, String>: if args.is_empty() { return Err(USAGE.to_string()); } let mut sum = 0i64; for arg in args { let Ok(num) = arg.parse::<i64>() else { return Err(USAGE.to_string()); }; let Some(next) = sum.checked_add(num) else { return Err("Error: Sum would overflow i64".to_string()); }; sum = next; } Ok(sum). Remove every FromStr import and i64::from_str call. Tests call parse_and_sum directly: vec!["1".to_string(), "2".to_string(), "3".to_string()] is Ok(6); negatives; vec![] is Err(USAGE); vec!["a".to_string()] is Err(USAGE); vec![i64::MAX.to_string(), i64::MAX.to_string()] is Err overflow message. No process spawning.
